definition_zh: 宠物；抚摸；宠爱的；宠儿
definition_en: an animal kept for company and pleasure; to touch an animal gently with the hand; kept or loved as a favourite
core_image: 一只猫把头拱进摊开的手掌，尾巴慢慢绕上人的手腕
scene: 傍晚的公园长椅上，一个人蹲下来，把手慢慢伸向瑟瑟发抖的小狗。 He waited until the dog stopped shaking, then began to pet it.
sceneCN: 这里 pet 是「抚摸（动物）」（第 2 个义项：用手轻轻反复摸）；句意为他等到小狗不再发抖，才伸手去摸它。图中可辨识物件：长椅、牵引绳、摊开的手掌。

derivatives.zh: 由 pet 加 -ing 构成，义为「抚摸；爱抚」
由 pet 与 sitter 复合而成，义为「代人照看宠物的人」
由 pet 与 friendly 复合而成，义为「对宠物友好的」

senses.title: An animal kept for company
senses.definition: a tame animal that someone keeps at home for pleasure and companionship rather than for work or food
senses.definitionCN: 养在家里供人陪伴取乐、而非用于干活或食用的驯养动物
senses.example: Their pet rabbit sleeps under the kitchen table.
senses.exampleCN: 他们家的宠物兔睡在厨房桌子底下。
senses.why: The word first named a lamb or a child that had been tamed and spoiled, so the animal sense grows out of the idea of a creature brought close to the household.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早指被驯服、被宠着的小羊或孩子，所以「宠物」这个义项是从「被带进家门、养在近旁的活物」这个想法里长出来的。

senses.title: To stroke an animal gently
senses.definition: to touch an animal softly and repeatedly with the hand, as a sign of affection
senses.definitionCN: 用手轻柔而反复地触碰动物，表示亲昵
senses.example: She petted the cat until it purred.
senses.exampleCN: 她一直摸着那只猫，直到它发出呼噜声。
senses.why: Once a pet is the animal you keep close, the verb pet names the gesture that keeps it close: the hand repeats the same small movement.
senses.whyCN: 既然 pet 指被养在近旁的动物，动词 pet 就指让它留在近旁的那个动作：手掌一次次重复同一个小幅度的移动。

senses.title: Kept or loved as a favourite
senses.definition: used before a noun for something kept or chosen out of special affection or personal interest
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，表示因特别的喜爱或个人的兴趣而被保留、被选中的事物
senses.example: His pet project is a garden behind the school.
senses.exampleCN: 他最钟爱的项目是学校后面的一块园地。
senses.why: The adjective keeps only the favourite half of the noun and drops the animal, so any chosen thing, from a scheme to a subject, can become a pet one.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只保留名词中「受宠、偏爱」的那一半，丢掉了动物，于是任何被选中的东西，从方案到题目，都能变成「宠爱的」。

senses.title: A person who is specially favoured
senses.definition: a person treated with special kindness or favour, sometimes when others feel it is unfair
senses.definitionCN: 受到特别照顾或偏爱、有时让别人觉得不公平的人
senses.example: She was the teacher's pet and the class knew it.
senses.exampleCN: 她是老师的宠儿，全班都看得出来。
senses.why: If a pet is a creature indulged at home, the same word can label a person indulged inside a group, with a hint that the favour was not earned.
senses.whyCN: 如果 pet 是在家里被惯着的活物，同一个词就能用来标注在群体里被惯着的人，还带着「这份偏爱并非挣来的」那层暗示。

intro.en: The origin of pet is uncertain: it is first recorded in Scotland and northern England, and the usual Gaelic explanation is not settled.
intro.cn: pet 的来源不确定：它最早见于苏格兰与英格兰北部，常见的盖尔语解释也并未定论。

items.en: Pet is first recorded in the sixteenth century in Scotland and northern England for a tame, spoiled lamb or child.
items.cn: pet 最早在十六世纪见于苏格兰与英格兰北部，指被驯养、被惯着的小羊或孩子。

items.en: A common explanation derives it from Gaelic peata, a tame animal or a spoiled child, but the source is uncertain and the direction of borrowing is still debated.
items.cn: 一种常见的解释认为它来自盖尔语 peata（温顺的动物或受宠的孩子），但来源不确定，借入的方向至今仍有争论。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the noun had produced a verb meaning to treat as a pet, and from that to stroke an animal with the hand.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，这个名词已经生出动词用法，意为「当作宠物来养」，再由这里引申为「用手抚摸动物」。

items.en: The attributive use settled in the nineteenth century, in phrases such as pet dog and pet project.
items.cn: 作定语用的用法在十九世纪固定下来，出现于「宠物狗」「钟爱的项目」这类短语中。

items.en: Modern English keeps the animal at the centre, while teacher's pet and pet project carry the older idea of favouritism.
items.cn: 现代英语仍以动物义为中心，而「老师的宠儿」「钟爱的项目」则保留了更早那层「偏爱」的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same short stem plus one word that only looks similar; the near-meaning group collects words for touching and for being favoured.
note.cn: 形近组收同一短词干上的形式，外加一个只是拼写相近的词；近义组收表示「触摸」与「受偏爱」的词。

entries.definition: The act of stroking an animal gently.
Someone paid to look after a pet while its owner is away.
entries.definitionCN: 主人外出时受雇照看宠物的人。

entries.definition: A dark brown material formed from decayed plants and burned as fuel; it is only close in spelling, with a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 由腐烂植物形成的深褐色燃料；与目标词只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To move a hand slowly and gently over something.
entries.definitionCN: 用手缓慢轻柔地从某物上抚过。

entries.definition: To touch someone or something gently and lovingly.
entries.definitionCN: 温柔而充满爱意地触摸。

entries.definition: A person or thing liked more than others of the same kind.
entries.definitionCN: 同类中比别人更受喜欢的人或物。

entries.definition: To treat someone with too much kindness and protection.

normalIntro.en: A short word of uncertain origin, pet holds an animal, a hand and a favourite in one syllable.
normalIntro.cn: pet 是个来源不确定的短词，却在一个音节里同时装下了动物、手掌和偏爱。

normal.en: The word is first recorded in Scotland for a spoiled lamb, so a pet is an animal brought close and indulged, not simply any animal.
normal.cn: 这个词最早见于苏格兰，指被惯着的小羊，所以宠物是被带在身边宠着的动物，而不只是随便一只动物。

normal.en: The verb comes from the noun: to pet is to do for an animal what a pet receives, namely gentle handling.
normal.cn: 动词从名词来：抚摸动物，就是给宠物它惯常得到的那种轻柔摆弄。

normal.en: The adjective keeps only the favourite half, so a pet project has no animal in it at all.
normal.cn: 形容词只保留「偏爱」那一半，所以「钟爱的项目」里根本没有动物。

normal.en: Petted and petting double the t, because the stress falls on the single final syllable.
normal.cn: petted 与 petting 都要双写 t，因为重音落在唯一的末尾音节上。

normal.en: Teacher's pet carries a warning: being one person's favourite can make the rest of the group resent you.
normal.cn: 「老师的宠儿」带着警告意味：成为某一个人的偏爱对象，可能招来其余人的不满。

abstract.en: A warm weight settling on your lap holds the noun and the verb in a single picture.
abstract.cn: 一团温暖的重量落在腿上，名词和动词就在这一幅画里。

abstract.en: The word is short and soft and ends in a light tap, like a hand touching fur twice.
abstract.cn: 这个词短而软，结尾像轻轻一叩，如同手掌在毛上碰了两下。

abstract.en: English spends one syllable on the animal, the touch and the favour, because all three happen in the same small space.
abstract.cn: 英语用一个音节同时承担动物、触摸和偏爱，因为这三件事本来就发生在同一小块空间里。

examples.en: The children were allowed to pet the ponies at the fair.
examples.cn: 在集市上，孩子们获准去摸那些小马。

examples.en: A pet can cost more than people expect.
examples.cn: 养一只宠物可能比人们预想的更花钱。

examples.en: Her pet subject is the history of the harbour.
examples.cn: 她最偏爱的题目是这座港口的历史。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拍它」——轻轻拍它，就是抚摸宠物；pet 既指宠物，也指拍它的那个动作。

root: 来源不确定。一般认为最早见于苏格兰与英格兰北部，指被驯养、受宠的小羊或孩子；常见解释是来自盖尔语 peata（温顺的动物、受宠的孩子），但借入方向仍有争论；无可靠拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a tame creature kept close and indulged; from it come the hand that keeps it close, the thing chosen out of favour, and the person who is someone's favourite.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被养在近旁、受着宠的驯养活物；由此长出「让它留在近旁的手」、「因偏爱而选中的东西」，以及「某人的宠儿」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cat pushing its head into an open palm, its tail curling round the wrist.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只猫把头拱进摊开的手掌，尾巴慢慢绕上手腕。

branches.cn: 睡在厨房桌下的兔子

branches.cn: 总被第一个叫到前排的学生

branches.en: a name written at the top of somebody's list
branches.cn: 被写在某人名单最上面的名字

definition_zh: 高兴的；乐意的；令人高兴的
definition_en: pleased and happy about something, or willing to do something for someone
core_image: 脸上忽然亮起来的笑意：事情合了心意
scene: 收到录取通知的那天早晨，她一路小跑回了家。 She was glad to hear that she had passed the exam.
sceneCN: 这里 glad 是「高兴的；欣慰的」（第 1 个义项：为某事感到愉快）；句意为她高兴地得知自己通过了考试。

pos.zh: 高兴的；乐意的；令人高兴的

derivatives.zh: 由 glad 加 -en 构成，义为「使高兴」
由 glad 加 -ly 构成，义为「乐意地」
由 glad 加 -ness 构成，义为「高兴；喜悦」

senses.title: Pleased about something
senses.definition: feeling pleased and happy because something has happened
senses.definitionCN: 因某事发生而感到愉快
senses.example: She was glad to hear that she had passed the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 她高兴地得知自己通过了考试。
senses.why: The core image is a face lighting up when things go your way, the plain everyday feeling.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是事情顺心时脸上亮起的神色，是最日常的情绪。

senses.title: Willing and ready to help
senses.definition: very willing to do something for someone
senses.definitionCN: 非常愿意为某人做某事
senses.example: I am glad to help you carry the boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 我很乐意帮你搬箱子。
senses.why: A happy heart says yes easily, so gladness slides into willingness.
senses.whyCN: 心情好的人 easily 点头，高兴便滑向乐意。

senses.title: Bringing joy to others
senses.definition: causing happiness to others, in older phrases like glad news or glad day
senses.definitionCN: 使他人快乐的，用于 glad news 等旧式表达
senses.example: The glad news spread through the village at once.
senses.exampleCN: 好消息立刻传遍了全村。
senses.why: The feeling a face shows can be given away, so events and news can be glad too.
senses.whyCN: 脸上的情绪可以传染给他人，于是消息与日子也可以是 glad 的。

senses.title: Bright and joyful in look
senses.definition: shining with joy, describing looks, eyes or sounds in literary use
senses.definitionCN: 闪耀喜悦光彩的，书面语中形容眼神、声音
senses.example: She welcomed them with glad eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 她用欢悦的目光迎接他们。
senses.why: Joy is visible light on a face, so eyes and days can carry gladness like colour.
senses.whyCN: 喜悦像脸上的光，眼神与日子便都能带上这份亮色。

intro.en: Glad once meant bright and shining; happiness was imagined as light.
intro.cn: glad 曾意为明亮闪耀，快乐被想象成光。

items.en: The reconstructed root gladh- meant smooth and bright.
items.cn: 重构词根 gladh- 意为平滑、明亮。

items.en: Old English glæd meant bright, shining and also joyful.
items.cn: 古英语 glæd 意为明亮的，兼指喜悦的。

items.en: Middle English glad leaned toward the feeling of joy, keeping the bright metaphor.
items.cn: 中古英语 glad 偏向喜悦之情，保留了明亮的比喻。

items.en: Norse gladr, meaning bright and cheerful, is a close relative in the same family.
items.cn: 诺斯语 gladr 意为明快欢悦，是同族中的近亲。

items.en: Modern English settled glad on pleased and willing, while gladness and gladden survived.
items.cn: 现代英语把 glad 定在高兴与乐意，gladness 与 gladden 得以留存。

note.en: The words below sound like glad or share its field of happiness.
note.cn: 以下词与 glad 音近，或同属快乐义场。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「林间空地」，与 glad 仅差一个字母，词义无关。

entries.definition: Willingly and happily.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「乐意地」，由 glad 直接派生。

entries.definition: Informal short for graduate; sounds close.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，graduates 的口语缩写，读音与 glad 接近。

entries.definition: Feeling or showing pleasure; the everyday general word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「快乐的」，最常用的日常说法。

entries.definition: Very pleased about something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「欣喜的」，程度比 glad 更强。

entries.definition: Happy in a way that shows in behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「兴高采烈的」，强调外显的情绪。

normalIntro.en: Five links to real forms and uses of glad.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实构形与用法的联想。

normal.en: Old English glæd meant bright as well as happy; joy was imagined as light.
normal.cn: 古英语 glæd 兼指明亮与快乐，喜悦被想象成光。

normal.en: German still has glatt for smooth, a cousin keeping the original sense.
normal.cn: 德语 glatt 意为光滑，保留了原始义的亲属词。

normal.en: Gladden is the verb that makes someone glad.
normal.cn: gladden 是使人高兴的动词。

normal.en: Glad to help is a polite set phrase in daily speech.
normal.cn: glad to help 是日常礼貌用语。

normal.en: Gladness is the noun for the state of being glad.

abstract.en: Picture a grey morning face turning bright the moment good news lands.
abstract.cn: 想象灰暗的晨脸在好消息落地的一瞬亮起来。

abstract.en: See a smile spread quickly before the mind even explains why.
abstract.cn: 想象笑容先于理由飞快展开。

abstract.en: Think of light sliding across a floor when a curtain is pulled open.
abstract.cn: 想象窗帘拉开时光线滑过地板。

examples.cn: 她高兴地得知自己通过了考试。

examples.en: The glad news spread through the village at once.
examples.cn: 好消息立刻传遍了全村。

sensesIntro.cn: glad 从感到愉快延伸到乐意、给予快乐与散发光彩。

branches.cn: 考试通过后的欣慰

intro.cn: glad 是日耳曼基础形容词，下面列出它的词尾与短语。

definition_zh: 放；放置；表达；使处于某种状态；推迟
definition_en: to move something into a position and leave it there; to express something in words; to cause someone or something to be in a state; in put off, to delay
core_image: 一只手把杯子稳稳放到桌面上，随即松开
scene: 夜深了，母亲把洗好的碗一只只擦干，转身走向橱柜。 She put the plates on the top shelf and closed the door.
sceneCN: 这里 put 是「放置」（第 1 个义项：把东西放到某处）；句意为她把盘子放到最上层架子上，然后关上柜门。画面里可留意：擦干的碗、橱柜、最上层架子。

pos.zh: 放；放置；表达；使处于；推迟

derivatives.zh: in 与 put 复合，指放进系统的内容，即输入
out 与 put 复合，指系统送出的结果，即产出
put 与 down 复合，指把人压低的话，即贬损
put 与 on 复合，指装出来的样子，即做作

senses.title: To place something somewhere
senses.definition: to move something into a position and leave it there
senses.definitionCN: 把某物移到某个位置并留在那里
senses.example: She put the keys beside the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她把钥匙放在门边。
senses.why: The earliest recorded sense is simply to set a thing down and let go, and almost every other sense grows out of that picture.
senses.whyCN: 有记录的最早义项就是把东西放下然后松手，其余义项几乎都从这幅画面长出来。

senses.title: To express something in words
senses.definition: to say or write something in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式说出或写出某事
senses.example: How should I put this so nobody is hurt?
senses.exampleCN: 这话我该怎么说才不伤人？
senses.why: Words are placed into a sentence the way objects are placed on a table, so arranging language took the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 词被安放进句子，就像东西被摆到桌面上，于是「安排语言」也用了同一个动词。

senses.title: To cause someone to be in a state
senses.definition: to cause someone or something to be in a particular situation or condition
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物进入某种处境或状态
senses.example: The new rule put everyone under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定让每个人都感到了压力。
senses.why: If a thing can be placed in a spot, a person can be placed in a condition, and the verb then means to bring that condition about.
senses.whyCN: 东西既能被放到某个位置，人也能被放进某种处境，于是这个动词就表示「使某种处境发生」。

senses.title: To delay something, in put off
senses.definition: in the phrasal verb put off, to move an event or an action to a later time
senses.definitionCN: 在短语动词 put off 中，把一件事或一个行动挪到以后
senses.example: They put off the meeting until Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把会议推迟到周五。
senses.why: Putting a thing off is putting it away from the present moment, so the spatial verb turns into a verb about time.
senses.whyCN: 把一件事推开，就是把它从当下这一刻挪走，于是空间上的动词转成了时间上的动词。

intro.en: The origin of put is uncertain. It is first recorded in Middle English, and it may come from Old English, from Old Norse pota, or from Old French bouter, all of which suggest a gesture of thrusting or placing; no reliable Latin cognate exists.
intro.cn: put 的来源不确定。它最早见于中古英语，可能来自古英语，也可能来自古诺斯语 pota 或古法语 bouter，这些说法都与「推、放」的手势有关；它没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: Old Norse pota meant to poke or thrust, and it is one of the forms often suggested as a source; the link is possible rather than proved.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 pota 意为戳、推，是常被提出的来源之一；这只是可能，并未得到确证。

items.en: Some scholars reconstruct an Old English verb putian, but it is not attested in surviving texts, so it remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: 有学者为古英语重构出动词 putian，但现存文献中并无此词，所以它仍只是假说。

items.en: Old French bouter meant to thrust or shove and may have reinforced the English word, especially in southern dialects.
items.cn: 古法语 bouter 意为推、顶，可能在英格兰南部方言中加强了这个英语词。

items.en: Middle English putten is recorded from the fourteenth century with the sense of placing something somewhere.
items.cn: 中古英语 putten 自十四世纪起有记录，意为把某物放到某处。

items.en: Modern English keeps the irregular past put and builds a wide range of phrasal verbs such as put off, put up with and put forward.
items.cn: 现代英语保留不规则的过去式 put，并构成 put off、put up with、put forward 等大量短语动词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds built with put and a few words that only look similar; the near-meaning group collects other verbs of placing.
note.cn: 形近组收由 put 构成的复合词以及几个只是外形相近的词；近义组收其他表示放置的动词。

entries.definition: What a system produces after processing its input.
entries.definitionCN: 系统处理输入之后产生的结果。

entries.definitionCN: 高尔夫中的轻推击球；这个词来自苏格兰语，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To place an object carefully in a chosen spot.

To arrange something deliberately for a purpose.

normalIntro.en: The word has one unchanging past form, and its many phrasal verbs all move things in space or in time.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的过去式只有一种写法，而它的大量短语动词都在空间或时间里挪动东西。

normal.en: Put keeps the same form for the past, so only the rest of the sentence tells you when it happened.
normal.cn: put 的过去式与原型同形，只能靠句子的其余部分判断时间。

normal.en: Input and output are put with in and out: what is put in and what is put out.
normal.cn: input 与 output 就是 put 加 in 与 out：放进去的东西与送出来的东西。

normal.en: A put-down is a remark that places a person lower than they stood a moment before.
normal.cn: put-down 是一句话，把一个人放到比片刻之前更低的位置。

normal.en: Put off moves an event away from now, while put up with means to hold up under something.
normal.cn: put off 把一件事挪离当下，put up with 则是把某件事忍下来。

normal.en: Learners often master this verb last because every regular ending would sound wrong to a native ear.
normal.cn: 学习者往往最后才掌握这个动词，因为任何规则变化的词尾在本族语者听来都不对。

abstract.en: To put is to decide where a thing belongs, if only for the next minute.
abstract.cn: 放，就是决定一样东西该在哪儿，哪怕只为下一分钟。

abstract.en: Every sentence is a row of things put in order, which is why one verb serves both the table and the tongue.
abstract.cn: 每个句子都是把东西排好的一行，所以同一个动词既管桌面也管舌头。

abstract.en: Putting something off is storing it in the future, and the future is where unfinished things collect.
abstract.cn: 把事情推迟，就是把它存进未来，而未完成的事总在未来堆积。

examples.en: Please put the chairs back where you found them.
examples.cn: 请把椅子放回你原来找到的地方。

examples.en: She put her objection in the mildest words she could find.
examples.cn: 她用能找到的最温和的说法表达了反对。

examples.en: The match was put off because of the storm.
examples.cn: 比赛因暴风雨推迟了。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a hand setting an object down; the senses divide into placing, wording, causing a state, and moving something into the future.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是一只手把物体放下；义项由此分为放置、措辞、使进入某种状态，以及把某事挪到以后。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand setting a cup firmly on a table, then letting go.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把杯子稳稳放到桌面上，随即松开。

branches.en: a cup set down and released
branches.cn: 放下并松开手的杯子

branches.en: a sentence built like a shelf

branches.en: a person standing inside a new rule
branches.cn: 站在新规定里的人

branches.en: a meeting moved to another page of the calendar
branches.cn: 被挪到日历另一页的会议

branches.en: the same hand moving things in space and in time
branches.cn: 同一只手在空间与时间里挪动东西

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; the forms behind it are Germanic and Romance, and its origin is uncertain.

definition_zh: 触摸；接触；触觉；少量；联系；感动；涉及
definition_en: to put a hand or an object lightly against something, or the act and sense of such contact
core_image: 指尖轻轻碰到冰凉的玻璃，只留下一圈几乎看不见的雾
scene: 展厅里隔着护栏，讲解员举起手示意不许靠近。 Please do not touch the paintings on the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 touch 是动词「触摸、碰」（第 1 个义项：用手或物体轻触某物）；句意为请不要触摸墙上的画。画面里有护栏、伸出的手与墙上的画框。

pos.zh: 动词：触摸；碰到；感动；涉及
名词：触摸；触觉；少量；联系

derivatives.zh: 加 -ing 构成，义为「动人的；感人的」
加 -ed 构成，义为「感动的；有点疯的（口语）」
加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「未触动过的；未受影响的」
拉丁同源形容词，义为「触觉的」

senses.title: To put a hand on something
senses.definition: to put a hand or finger on something, especially lightly
senses.definitionCN: 用手或手指轻放在某物上，尤指轻轻地
senses.example: She touched the cold glass to feel where the crack began.
senses.exampleCN: 她摸着冰凉的玻璃，想找出裂纹从何处开始。
senses.why: The French verb tocher gave English a word for the light contact of one thing on another.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词 tocher 为英语提供了表示一物与另一物轻触的词。

senses.title: An act of contact
senses.definition: the state or act of two things being in contact
senses.definitionCN: 两物相互接触的状态或动作
senses.example: A single touch of the wire set off the alarm.
senses.exampleCN: 电线被碰了一下，警报就响了。
senses.why: The verb and the noun are the same idea seen from two sides, one as action and one as event.
senses.whyCN: 动词与名词是同一概念的两面，一为动作，一为事件。

senses.title: The sense of feeling
senses.definition: the ability of the skin to feel what comes against it
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤感知接触物的能力
senses.example: After the accident he lost the touch in two fingers.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后他两根手指失去了触觉。
senses.why: Among the five senses, touch is the one that works only by direct contact, which is why the word names it.
senses.whyCN: 五官之中，触觉是唯一靠直接接触起作用的，这个词正因此用来命名它。

senses.title: A small amount
senses.definition: a very small quantity of something, often added to a dish or a colour
senses.definitionCN: 极少的一点，常指添进菜肴或颜色的部分
senses.example: Add a touch of salt to the soup before serving.
senses.exampleCN: 上桌前在汤里加一点盐。
senses.why: A small amount is like a fingertip of something, just enough to be felt but not taken in bulk.
senses.whyCN: 少量就像指尖沾到的那一点，感觉得到，却谈不上分量。

senses.title: Contact between people
senses.definition: the state of communicating with someone, as in keep in touch
senses.definitionCN: 与人保持交流的状态，如 keep in touch
senses.example: We stayed in touch after we left the same school.
senses.exampleCN: 离开同一所学校后我们一直保持联系。
senses.why: People who correspond are in contact even at a distance, so the physical word carries over to communication.
senses.whyCN: 保持来往的人即便相隔也处于「接触」中，于是物理的词被挪用到交流上。

senses.title: To move someone deeply
senses.definition: to cause a strong feeling of sympathy or gratitude
senses.definitionCN: 引起强烈的同情或感激之情
senses.example: The letter from her old teacher touched her more than any gift.
senses.exampleCN: 老教师的那封信比任何礼物都让她感动。
senses.why: A feeling is said to reach the heart as a hand reaches the skin, so being moved is being touched.
senses.whyCN: 情感像手触到皮肤那样抵达心里，所以被感动就是被 touch 到。

senses.title: To deal with a subject
senses.definition: to mention or deal with a matter briefly
senses.definitionCN: 简短地提到或处理某个问题
senses.example: The report touches on housing but says little about cost.
senses.exampleCN: 报告谈及住房，却很少提到成本。
senses.why: To touch a subject is to come into contact with it lightly, without taking it up fully.
senses.whyCN: touch 一个话题就是轻轻碰到它，并不把它完全展开。

senses.title: A slight trace of a quality
senses.definition: a slight trace of a quality, as in a touch of sadness
senses.definitionCN: 某种特质的一丝痕迹，如 a touch of sadness
senses.example: There was a touch of frost on the windows this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 今早窗上有一层薄霜。
senses.why: The sense of a small quantity extends from food to weather and to mood, wherever a trace can be noticed.
senses.whyCN: 「少量」义从食物扩展到天气与心情，凡是能察觉出痕迹的地方都能用。

senses.title: Skill with the hands
senses.definition: a special skill in handling something, as in the common touch or a fine touch
senses.definitionCN: 处理某物时的特别本领，如 the common touch 或 a fine touch
senses.example: The old cook still had a fine touch with pastry.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老厨子做起酥点来仍然手法精到。
senses.why: Skill shows in how the hand meets the material, so a good worker is said to have a good touch.
senses.whyCN: 手艺体现在手与材料相接的方式上，所以好手艺被说成有好的 touch。

senses.title: In football and rugby
senses.definition: in rugby and some other games, the area at the side of the field, or the act of grounding the ball
senses.definitionCN: 在橄榄球等运动中指场边区域，或把球触地的动作
senses.example: The ball went into touch and the line-out followed.
senses.exampleCN: 球出了边线，随后进行边线掷球。
senses.why: The sporting use keeps the literal sense: the ball leaves the field by touching the boundary.
senses.whyCN: 体育用法保留了字面义：球碰到边线而离开场地。

intro.en: Touch comes from Old French tochier, from a Vulgar Latin verb built on a root meaning to knock or strike, and it has been used for both contact and feeling since the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: touch 来自古法语 tochier，其源是表示「敲、击」词根的通俗拉丁语动词；自中世纪以来既指接触，也指感受。

items.en: A Vulgar Latin verb related to toccare means to knock or strike lightly against something.
items.cn: 与 toccare 相关的通俗拉丁语动词意为轻敲或轻击某物。

items.en: Old French tochier carries the senses of touching, tasting, and trying.
items.cn: 古法语 tochier 兼有触摸、品尝与尝试诸义。

items.en: Middle English touchen appears in the thirteenth century for physical contact.
items.cn: 中古英语 touchen 在十三世纪出现，表示身体上的接触。

items.en: The sense of moving the feelings is recorded early, since the heart was thought to be struck by emotion.
items.cn: 「感动」义很早就有了，因为当时认为情感会击中心。

items.en: The phrase keep in touch grows out of the older idea of hands meeting in greeting.
items.cn: keep in touch 这一说法源自更早的「以手相握致意」的想法。

items.en: Touch screens and touch typing make the word name any contact used to give a command.
items.cn: 触摸屏与盲打让这个词指任何用来下达指令的接触。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivative and compound forms, while the near-meaning group gathers verbs for contact and for feeling.
note.cn: 形近组收集派生与复合形式，近义组则汇集表示接触与感受的动词。

normal.en: Keep in touch is about writing and calling, not about hands.
normal.cn: keep in touch 说的是写信打电话，与手无关。

normal.en: A touch of salt and a touch of frost both mean a very small amount.
normal.cn: a touch of salt 与 a touch of frost 都指极少的一点。

normal.en: Touch on a subject means to mention it lightly, never to treat it fully.
normal.cn: touch on a subject 指轻轻提到，从不彻底处理。

normal.en: In rugby, the ball goes into touch when it crosses the side line.
normal.cn: 在橄榄球中，球越过边线就叫出 touch。

normal.en: The adjective touching keeps the feeling sense: a touching story moves you.
normal.cn: 形容词 touching 保留感受义：a touching story 让你感动。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip on cold glass and the faint print it leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖按在冰凉的玻璃上，留下淡淡的印。

abstract.en: Think of two wires just meeting, and the whole machine starting up.
abstract.cn: 想两根线刚刚接上，整台机器就启动了。

abstract.en: One light contact is enough to carry either information or feeling.
abstract.cn: 轻轻一次接触，就足以传递信息，也足以传递情感。

examples.en: Do not touch the wet paint on the bench.
examples.cn: 别碰长椅上还没干的油漆。

examples.en: We lost touch for years and then met again at a wedding.
examples.cn: 我们失联多年，后来在一场婚礼上重逢。

examples.en: Her speech touched everyone in the hall.
examples.cn: 她的演讲感动了礼堂里的每一个人。

definition_zh: 压力；强调；重音
definition_en: worry caused by a difficult situation, special importance given to something, or the stronger sound in a word
core_image: 一根被拉紧的弦，绷得快要发出声音
scene: 考试前他感到很大压力。 He felt a lot of stress before the exam.
sceneCN: 这里 stress 是「压力」（第 1 个义项）；句意：考试前他感到很大压力。

derivatives.zh: 有压力的；紧张的
紧张的；焦虑的
压力源

senses.title: Mental pressure
senses.definition: worry and tension caused by a difficult situation
senses.definitionCN: 困难处境造成的担忧与紧张
senses.example: He felt a lot of stress before the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前他感到很大压力。
senses.why: This is pressure on the mind.
senses.whyCN: 这是压在心里的压力。

senses.title: Special emphasis
senses.definition: special importance given to something
senses.definitionCN: 给予某事物的特别重视
senses.example: The teacher stressed the need for rest.
senses.exampleCN: 老师强调了休息的必要。
senses.why: The mind presses on one point.
senses.whyCN: 心思在这里压住了一个重点。

senses.title: Strong sound
senses.definition: the stronger sound in a word or phrase
senses.definitionCN: 单词或短语中读得更强的音
senses.example: Put the stress on the first syllable.
senses.exampleCN: 把重音放在第一个音节上。
senses.why: Voice pressure marks the beat.
senses.whyCN: 声音的力度标出了节拍。

intro.en: Stress comes from distress, from Old French destrece, narrowness or hardship.
intro.cn: stress 由 distress 截短而来，源自法语 destrece，意为狭窄与艰难。

items.en: Strictus meant drawn tight.
items.cn: strictus 意为拉紧的。

items.en: Destrece named hardship and tightness.
items.cn: destrece 指艰难与紧绷。

items.en: Distresse named great trouble.
items.cn: 中古英语 distresse 指巨大的困苦。

items.en: Stress shortened the word and kept the pressure.
items.cn: stress 截短了词形，保留了压力之意。

items.en: It also named vocal emphasis.
items.cn: 它也开始指语音上的重音。

note.en: Stress is compared with look-alike words and with words for pressure.

normalIntro.en: Stress is a tightened string, whether in the mind, the voice, or the sentence.
normalIntro.cn: stress 是一根绷紧的弦，可能在心里、在声音里，也可能在句子里。

normal.en: Too much stress harms sleep.
normal.cn: 压力过大会损害睡眠。

normal.en: She stressed the value of teamwork.
normal.cn: 她强调了团队合作的价值。

normal.en: The word has stress on the second syllable.
normal.cn: 这个词的重音在第二个音节。

normal.en: He is under great stress at work.
normal.cn: 他工作时承受着巨大压力。

normal.en: Do not stress out over small things.
normal.cn: 别为小事紧张不安。

abstract.en: Stress is weight the mind puts on itself.

definition_zh: 词；单词；话；消息；诺言
definition_en: a single unit of language that has a meaning, or a short remark, news, or a promise
core_image: 一个人张开嘴，一个音节落出来，另一个人的表情立刻变了
scene: 母亲只轻轻说了两个字，站在门口的孩子就放下手里的东西转身回了屋。 I did not catch a single word of what he said in the noisy hall.
sceneCN: 这里 word 是「词、说的话」（第 1 个义项：语言中能独立表意的最小单位）；句意是在嘈杂的大厅里我一句也没听清他说的话。一个音节落下、听者表情立刻改变，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 word 加 -y 构成，义为「话多的；冗长的」

senses.title: The unit of language
senses.definition: a single unit of speech or writing that carries a meaning of its own
senses.definitionCN: 口语或书面语中能独立承载意义的最小单位
senses.example: I did not catch a single word of what he said in the noisy hall.
senses.exampleCN: 在嘈杂的大厅里，他说的每一句话我都没听清。
senses.why: This is the literal core: one sound or one written group that stands for something.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面的核心：一串声音或一组字母，代表某个东西。

senses.title: Something said
senses.definition: a remark or statement, often a short one, taken as it was spoken
senses.definitionCN: 说出口的话或陈述，常常较短，按原样取用
senses.example: A word from her was enough to quiet the whole room.
senses.exampleCN: 她只说一句话，整个屋子就静了下来。
senses.why: Once a unit of language is spoken, it becomes an act in the world, so the word means the remark itself.
senses.whyCN: 语言单位一旦说出口，就成了世界中的一个动作，于是这个词也就指那句具体的话。

senses.title: News carried by speech
senses.definition: information passed from one person to another, usually in the phrase send word
senses.definitionCN: 从一人传到另一人的消息，常用于 send word 这一说法
senses.example: Word of the flood reached the village before the water did.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水的消息比水先到了村里。
senses.why: Because news travels by speech, the unit of speech came to stand for the news it carries.
senses.whyCN: 因为消息靠言语传递，说话的単位便代表它所承载的消息。

senses.title: A promise
senses.definition: a promise that one gives serious weight to, as in keep one's word
senses.definitionCN: 认真对待的承诺，如 keep one's word
senses.example: He gave his word that the work would be finished by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 他保证这项活儿周五之前完成。
senses.why: A spoken promise is only words, so the word itself became the deposit for trust.
senses.whyCN: 说出口的承诺只是言语，于是这个词本身成了信任的抵押。

senses.title: The way something is put
senses.definition: the particular choice of words used to express something, as in the wording of a rule
senses.definitionCN: 表达某事时的具体用词选择，如条文的措辞
senses.example: The lawyer asked for a change in the word order of the clause.
senses.exampleCN: 律师要求改一下这一条款的词序。
senses.why: Where the unit of language is arranged and chosen, the word names the arrangement as well.
senses.whyCN: 语言单位被挑选与排列的地方，这个词便也指那种排列。

intro.en: Word is Old English word, shared with German Wort and Dutch woord, and originally meant a spoken utterance before it meant a unit of grammar.
intro.cn: word 来自古英语 word，与德语 Wort、荷兰语 woord 同源，最初指说出口的话语，后来才指语法单位。

items.en: word meant a spoken utterance or a message, not a unit on a page.
items.cn: word 指说出口的话或一条信息，不是纸上的一处单位。

items.en: The same noun appears in the other Germanic languages with the same sense.
items.cn: 同一名词在其他日耳曼语里出现，意思相同。

items.en: Latin verbum was the model for grammar writing, which helped the unit sense grow.
items.cn: 拉丁语 verbum 是语法写作的样板，帮助了「单位」这一义项的生长。

items.en: The spelling took its r after the vowel, and word was fixed in both senses, utterance and unit.
items.cn: 拼写把 r 放在元音之后，word 在「话语」与「单位」两义上固定下来。

items.en: The promise sense hardened in phrases such as keep one's word.
items.cn: 诺言之义在 keep one's word 之类的说法里凝定。

note.en: The first group holds the family of words built on this stem, the second holds other language units and speech terms.
note.cn: 第一组收由这个词干构成的词族，第二组收其他语言单位与言辞词。

definition_zh: 懒惰的；慵懒的；懒洋洋的；马虎的
definition_en: unwilling to work or make effort, pleasantly relaxed, slow and without force, or done without care
core_image: 午后斜阳照进院子，一个人摊在躺椅上，手边的杯子够不着也不愿起身
scene: 午后的院子里，躺椅上的人伸手够了够杯子，又把手放下。 It was a lazy afternoon, and nobody wanted to move.
sceneCN: 这里是「慵懒的、悠闲的」（第 2 个义项：轻松惬意、不费力的状态）；句意为那是一个慵懒的午后，没人愿意动。可辨识画面：斜阳、躺椅、手边的杯子。

pos.zh: 懒惰的；慵懒的；懒洋洋的；马虎的

derivatives.zh: 由 lazy 变 y 为 i 再加 -ly 构成，义为「懒洋洋地」
由 lazy 变 y 为 i 再加 -ness 构成，义为「懒惰」
由 lazy 与 bones 复合，义为「懒骨头」
一般认为由 lazy 逆构而成，义为「懒散地打发时间」

senses.title: Unwilling to work or make effort
senses.definition: not willing to work or to make any effort
senses.definitionCN: 不愿意工作或付出任何努力
senses.example: He is too lazy to wash his own cup.
senses.exampleCN: 他懒得连自己的杯子都不洗。
senses.why: The word probably came from a Low German term for weak or useless, so laziness began as a body that would not serve.
senses.whyCN: 这个词很可能来自低地德语中表示虚弱、无用的说法，所以懒惰最初是身体不肯出力。

senses.title: Pleasantly relaxed
senses.definition: relaxed and slow in a pleasant way, as of a warm afternoon
senses.definitionCN: 轻松而缓慢，令人愉快，如温暖的午后
senses.example: We spent a lazy afternoon by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在河边度过了一个慵懒的午后。
senses.why: If a body refuses effort, the same word can describe a time when no effort is asked for, and the refusal turns into comfort.
senses.whyCN: 身体若不肯出力，同一个词也能形容一段不需要出力的时间，拒绝就变成了惬意。

senses.title: Slow and without force
senses.titleCN: 懒洋洋的；缓慢不用力的
senses.definition: moving or flowing slowly, without energy
senses.definitionCN: 动作或流动缓慢，不带力气
senses.example: A lazy smile spread across his face.
senses.exampleCN: 他脸上浮起懒洋洋的笑。
senses.why: The idea of withheld effort moves easily onto movements and sounds, so slow and soft things are called lazy too.
senses.whyCN: 「不肯出力」的想法很容易挪到动作与声音上，于是缓慢柔和的东西也被说成 lazy。

senses.title: Careless, done without proper effort
senses.definition: done without care or attention, as a lazy attempt
senses.definitionCN: 做事不细心、不用心，如敷衍的尝试
senses.example: The report was a lazy piece of work.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告写得很敷衍。
senses.why: When effort is withheld from work that needs it, the word stops being pleasant and becomes a criticism of quality.
senses.whyCN: 当该出力的活被省了力气，这个词就不再惬意，而成了对质量的批评。

intro.en: This word has no known Old English form; it appears in the sixteenth century, probably from a Low German or Dutch term for weakness.
intro.cn: 这个词没有已知的古英语形态，十六世纪才出现，一般认为来自低地德语或荷兰语中表示虚弱说法。

items.en: No Old English form is known, so the path before the sixteenth century is uncertain.
items.cn: 没有已知的古英语形式，十六世纪之前的来路并不确定。

items.en: The word is first recorded in the sixteenth century, probably from a Low German or Dutch term for weak or useless.
items.cn: 这个词最早见于十六世纪，一般认为来自低地德语或荷兰语中表示虚弱、无用的说法。

items.en: English lazy appears first meaning disinclined to work, with the bodily sense of weakness still near.
items.cn: 英语 lazy 最初表示不愿干活，身体虚弱的意味还很近。

items.en: The pleasant sense of a relaxed time grows later, especially in phrases like a lazy afternoon.
items.cn: 「悠闲时光」的愉快义出现较晚，尤见于 a lazy afternoon 这类说法。

items.en: Modern English uses lazy for people, for comfortable slow time, and for work done without care.
items.cn: 现代英语用 lazy 形容人、形容舒适缓慢的时间，也形容不用心做出的活。

entries.definition: Not working or not in use.

entries.definition: Without energy or enthusiasm.

normal.en: Lazy has no known Old English form; it appears in the sixteenth century, probably from Low German or Dutch.
normal.cn: lazy 没有已知的古英语形式，十六世纪才出现，一般认为来自低地德语或荷兰语。

normal.en: Laze is a back-formation: the shorter verb was cut from the longer adjective.
normal.cn: laze 是逆构词：较短的动词是从较长的形容词上切下来的。

normal.en: Lazily and laziness change y to i before the suffix, as happy becomes happily.
normal.cn: lazily 与 laziness 在加后缀前把 y 变 i，就像 happy 变 happily。

normal.en: Lazybones is lazy plus bones, a joking name for a person who will not move.
normal.cn: lazybones 是 lazy 加 bones，是给不肯动的人起的玩笑称呼。

normal.en: A lazy afternoon is pleasant, but a lazy attempt is a criticism of the work.
normal.cn: a lazy afternoon 是惬意的，而 a lazy attempt 是对工作的批评。

abstract.en: The word began as a body that would not serve and ended as a description of comfort, a shift in who is judging.
abstract.cn: 这个词从「不肯出力的身体」走到「舒适的描述」，变的是谁在评判。

abstract.en: Calling a person lazy is a moral judgement, while calling an afternoon lazy is a gift of permission.
abstract.cn: 说一个人 lazy 是道德评判，而说一个午后 lazy 是允许人放松。

abstract.en: English separates the refusal of work from the need for rest by tone rather than by word.
abstract.cn: 英语用语气而不是用词，把「拒绝干活」与「需要休息」区分开。

examples.en: The report was a lazy piece of work.

definition_zh: 健康；健康状况；医疗；卫生
definition_en: the condition of your body and mind; how well someone is
core_image: 一棵浇水施肥后枝繁叶茂的树：状态良好、充满生机
scene: 体测那天他跑步、跳绳样样达标，医生夸他身体棒。 Good food and exercise keep him in good health.
sceneCN: 这里 health 是「健康」（第 1 个义项：身体与精神的良好状态）；饮食加锻炼让他状态良好，health 描述这种整体良好状况。

derivatives.zh: 健康的，由 health 加形容词后缀 -y 构成
健康地，由 healthy 加副词后缀 -ly 构成
治愈；愈合，与 health 同族，指使恢复健康

senses.title: The condition of body and mind
senses.definition: the general condition of a person's body and mind
senses.definitionCN: 一个人身体与精神的总体状况
senses.example: Regular sleep is the key to good health.
senses.exampleCN: 规律睡眠是健康的关键。
senses.why: The whole person runs well or badly like a machine, so health names that overall running state.
senses.whyCN: 整个人像机器一样运转良好或欠佳，health 命名的就是这种整体运转状态。

senses.title: The state of an organization or system

items.en: Old English hælth came from hal, meaning whole, sound, and uninjured.
items.cn: 古英语 hælth 出自 hal，意为「完整的、健全的、未受伤的」。

items.en: The root *hailaz meant whole or intact across the Germanic family.
items.cn: 词根 *hailaz 在日耳曼语族中意为「完整、完好」。

items.en: Old Norse heill, meaning good luck and soundness, reinforced the English sense.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 heill 意为「好运、健全」，强化了英语词义。

items.en: In Middle English, health also appeared in toasts, wishing others wholeness.
items.cn: 中古英语中 health 也出现在祝酒词里，祝愿他人安康。

items.en: Modern English built the medical sense, as in health care and public health.
items.cn: 现代英语发展出医疗义，如 health care、public health。

definition_zh: 机会；时机；机遇；就业或晋升的机会
definition_en: a chance to do something, a favourable moment or set of circumstances, or an opening for work and advancement
core_image: 一扇原本关着的门忽然被推开，门外透进一束亮光，正落在站着的人脚前
scene: 招聘会的走廊里挤满人，一个年轻人停在展位前，把手里那份改过三遍的简历递了出去。 She took the opportunity to ask the manager a direct question.
sceneCN: 这里的 opportunity 是「机会」（第 1 个义项：可以做某事的时机）；句意为她抓住机会直接向经理提了一个问题。图中可辨识物件：展位、简历、走廊人群。

pos.zh: 机会；时机；机遇；就业或晋升的机会

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 opportunus 而来，义为「恰好的；及时的」
由 opportune 加 -ism 构成，义为「机会主义；投机」
由 opportunist 加 -ic 构成，义为「投机取巧的；趁机的」

senses.title: A chance to do something
senses.definition: a situation in which it is possible for someone to do something they want or need to do
senses.definitionCN: 某人得以去做自己想做的事或必须做的事的境况
senses.example: She took the opportunity to ask the manager a direct question.
senses.exampleCN: 她抓住机会直接向经理提了一个问题。
senses.why: The word grew from a picture of a ship reaching a safe harbour, so a chance is imagined as a door that happens to be open just as you arrive.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从一个船靠上安全港湾的画面长出来，所以机会被想成一扇恰在你到达时敞开的门。

senses.title: A favourable moment
senses.definition: a short period that is especially suitable for acting, and which may not come again
senses.definitionCN: 特别适合行动的一段短时间，而且可能不会再来
senses.example: The quiet morning was the best opportunity to raise the matter.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的早晨是提这件事的最好时机。
senses.why: If the chance depends on the moment, then it can pass, and the word comes to mean the right hour rather than any possibility at all.
senses.whyCN: 既然机会取决于时刻，它就可能溜走，于是这个词指的是恰当的时刻，而不是任何可能性。

senses.title: Circumstances that favour success
senses.definition: a combination of conditions that makes progress or success more likely for someone
senses.definitionCN: 让某人更可能取得进展或成功的一组条件
senses.example: Growing up near the sea gave him opportunities his cousins never had.
senses.exampleCN: 在海边长大，给了他表兄弟们从未有过的机遇。
senses.why: Harbour and wind are conditions rather than actions, so the word also names the favourable state of things that lets a person move forward.
senses.whyCN: 港湾与风是条件而不是动作，所以这个词也指那种有利的境况，让人能够向前走。

senses.title: An opening for work or advancement
senses.definition: a post, vacancy or route by which someone may find work or move up
senses.definitionCN: 某人得以找到工作或向上发展的职位、空缺或门路
senses.example: The paper lists job opportunities every Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报纸每周日刊登招聘信息。
senses.why: A post that is open is literally a door left ajar, so employment and promotion are described with the same word as any other chance.
senses.whyCN: 一个空缺的职位本就是一扇虚掩的门，因此就业与晋升也用同一个词来描述，和其他机会并无分别。

intro.en: Opportunity comes from a Latin word for a wind that carries a ship toward harbour; the exact formation is generally explained as a phrase meaning toward the port, though some sources call it uncertain.
intro.cn: opportunity 来自拉丁语中表示「把船吹向港湾的风」的词；其构成一般认为出自意为「朝向港口」的说法，也有资料称来源不确定。

items.en: The usual explanation takes the source as ob portum, toward the harbour, the wind that lets a ship come safely in.
items.cn: 通常的解释把来源看作 ob portum，即「朝向港口」，指让船安全入港的那阵风。

items.en: From that phrase came opportunus, meaning favourable, timely or coming at the right moment, said first of winds and then of anything useful.
items.cn: 由这一短语得出 opportunus，意为有利的、适时的、来得正好的，先用于风，后用于任何合宜之物。

items.en: The noun opportunitas named the quality of being timely, and it could also mean a favourable opening or occasion.
items.cn: 名词 opportunitas 指「合宜」这种性质，也可指有利的时机或场合。

items.en: Old French carried the noun as opportunite, meaning a good chance or a suitable time, and English borrowed it with that practical sense.
items.cn: 古法语以 opportunite 承袭该名词，意为好机会或合适的时刻，英语借入时也带着这种实用的意味。

items.en: Modern English keeps opportunity for chances, for the right moment, for favourable conditions and for openings in work.
items.cn: 现代英语让 opportunity 兼指机会、恰当时刻、有利条件，以及工作上的空缺。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem of timeliness and harbour; the near-meaning group collects other names for a chance that can be used.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「合时、港湾」词干上的词；近义组收其他表示「可以利用的机会」的名称。

entries.definitionCN: 不顾原则地利用机会的做法。

entries.definitionCN: 利用一切机会谋取私利的人。

entries.definition: A possibility that something may happen or be done.
entries.definitionCN: 某事可能发生或可能做成的可能性。

entries.definition: A gap or vacancy that allows someone to enter or begin.

entries.definition: A particular time at which something happens or may happen.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生或可能发生的特定时刻。

entries.definition: A limited period during which action is possible.
entries.definitionCN: 可以采取行动的一段有限时期。

normalIntro.en: Opportunity began as weather and harbour talk, so its hooks keep a ship, a wind and an open door rather than any abstract idea of luck.
normalIntro.cn: opportunity 起初是谈天气与港湾的话，所以记忆钩子守着一艘船、一阵风和一道敞开的门，而不是抽象的运气。

normal.en: The Latin phrase behind the word means toward the harbour, and opportunus first described a wind that helped a ship in.
normal.cn: 这个词背后的拉丁短语意为「朝向港口」，opportunus 最初形容把船送进港的风。

normal.en: Opportune is the adjective, and opportunity is that adjective plus -ity, the suffix that turns a quality into a noun.
normal.cn: opportune 是形容词，opportunity 就是它加 -ity，这个后缀把一种性质变成名词。

normal.en: Seize the opportunity and a golden opportunity are fixed pairings: both treat the chance as something that can be grabbed or missed.
normal.cn: seize the opportunity 与 a golden opportunity 都是固定搭配：两者都把机会当成可以抓住或失去的东西。

normal.en: Equal opportunity is a phrase built on the same word, but it speaks of fairness rather than luck.
normal.cn: equal opportunity 也建立在同一个词上，但它讲的是公平，而不是运气。

normal.en: The spelling keeps double p and double t because both came from the Latin forms, so write opportunity with care.
normal.cn: 这个拼写保留双 p 与双 t，因为两者都来自拉丁形式，所以书写时要留意。

abstract.en: A word made from a harbour wind suggests that opportunity is not made but met, and only if you are ready to sail.
abstract.cn: 一个由港湾之风造出的词说明：机会不是被制造的，而是被遇上的，而且只有你准备好起航才算数。

abstract.en: Every chance carries an expiry, which is why the same word can mean a moment and a door.
abstract.cn: 每个机会都带着期限，所以同一个词既能指一段时刻，也能指一道门。

abstract.en: What looks like luck in one life is often a favourable set of conditions that someone else never had.
abstract.cn: 在一个人身上看似运气的东西，往往是一组别人从未拥有的有利条件。

definition_zh: 借口；理由（名词）；原谅；宽恕（动词）
definition_en: a reason given to explain a fault or to escape blame; to forgive or free someone from blame or a duty
core_image: 把责任从人肩上卸下来放到旁边：既可以是搬开真正的负担，也可以只是搬个说法
scene: 迟到的学生站在教室门口，书包还没放下就急着开口，老师摆摆手说： A heavy rain on the road is a reasonable excuse for being late.
sceneCN: 这里 excuse 指「用来脱责的理由」（第 1 个义项：为过错开脱的说法）；句意为路上大雨是迟到的合理解释。

senses.title: A reason offered to explain a fault
senses.definition: a reason given to explain or justify a mistake or failure
senses.definitionCN: 为错误或失败给出的解释或辩护理由
senses.example: A heavy rain on the road is a reasonable excuse for being late.
senses.exampleCN: 路上下大雨是迟到的合理解释。
senses.why: The Latin root is to hold blame away from someone: the story told does exactly this work for the person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根是「把罪责从某人身上拿开」：说出的说法正是在替人做这件事。

senses.title: A false or weak justification
senses.definition: a weak or untrue reason used to hide the real cause
senses.definitionCN: 用来掩盖真实原因的勉强或不实的理由
senses.example: Stop making excuses and start practising.

intro.en: Excuse goes back to Latin ex- (out) + causa (charge, accusation): literally to set the charge aside.
intro.cn: excuse 可追溯至拉丁语 ex-（向外）+ causa（指控）：字面义是「把指控挪开」。

items.en: Late Latin excusare meant "to free from blame", built on causa "a charge, a court case".
items.cn: 后期拉丁语 excusare 意为「使人免于罪责」，建立在 causa「指控、讼案」之上。

items.en: Causa also gave English cause; excuse is literally the act of removing a legal cause of complaint.
items.cn: causa 也衍生出英语 cause；excuse 字面上就是移除一桩法律上的控诉事由。

items.en: Old French excuser carried the verb into Romance speech with the same legal flavour.
items.cn: 古法语 excuser 以同样的法律色彩把动词带入罗曼语。

items.en: Middle English borrowed it in the thirteenth century, noun and verb arriving together.
items.cn: 十三世纪中古英语借入该词，名词与动词同时进入。

items.en: Modern English split the stress: EXcuse is the reason, exCUSE the forgiving act.
items.cn: 现代英语分化重音：EXcuse 是理由，exCUSE 是原谅的动作。

note.en: These neighbours share the spelling frame or the act of setting blame aside.
note.cn: 下列词与 excuse 拼写框架相同，或同样有「把责任放一边」的动作。

definition_zh: 陆地；土地；国土；登陆；着陆
definition_en: the solid surface of the earth, ground or a country, or to come down onto the ground
core_image: 船头前方浮出一条灰绿色的海岸线，脚下的甲板终于能换成泥土
scene: 飞机穿过云层，跑道在下方一点点变大。 The plane landed safely on the runway.
sceneCN: 这里是「着陆、降落」（第 4 个义项：动词，指飞行器触地停下）；句意为飞机安全地降落在跑道上。图中可辨识物件：云层、跑道、正在下降的飞机。

derivatives.zh: 由 land 加 -ing 构成，义为「着陆；登陆；楼梯平台」
由 land 与 -scape（景色）复合，义为「风景；景观」
由 land 与 lord 复合，义为「地主；房东」
由 main 与 land 复合，义为「大陆；本土」

senses.title: The solid surface of the earth
senses.definition: the part of the earth's surface that is not covered by water
senses.definitionCN: 地球表面没有被水覆盖的部分
senses.example: After weeks at sea, the sailors finally saw land.
senses.exampleCN: 在海上漂了几周之后，水手们终于看见了陆地。
senses.why: Land begins as the dry ground that a boat can reach, a boundary between water and solid earth.
senses.whyCN: land 最初指船只能抵达的干燥地面，是水与坚实大地之间的分界。

senses.title: Ground used for a purpose
senses.definition: ground owned or used by someone, especially for farming or building
senses.definitionCN: 某人拥有或使用的土地，尤指用于耕种或建造
senses.example: The family has farmed this land for three generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人在这块土地上耕种了三代。
senses.why: Once land means solid ground, it can be divided, owned and worked, so the word comes to mean a piece of ground with a use.
senses.whyCN: 既然 land 指坚实的地面，就可以被划分、拥有和耕作，于是它转而指一块有用途的地。

senses.title: A country or nation
senses.definition: a country, especially one thought of as the home of a people
senses.definitionCN: 国家，尤指被视为一个民族家园的国土
senses.example: She returned to her native land after many years abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 在国外多年之后，她回到了故土。
senses.why: A people's ground is their country, so land shifts from soil to the political and emotional idea of a homeland.
senses.whyCN: 一个民族脚下的土地就是他们的国家，于是 land 从泥土转到「故土」这一政治与情感概念。

senses.title: To come down to the ground
senses.definition: to come to the ground from the air or from water, especially after a flight
senses.definitionCN: 从空中或水上来到地面，尤指飞行之后
senses.example: The plane landed safely on the runway.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机安全地降落在跑道上。
senses.why: The noun names the ground; the verb reverses the direction and means reaching that ground, as a plane or a boat does.
senses.whyCN: 名词指地面；动词把方向反过来，表示抵达地面，飞机或船就是这样。

senses.title: To succeed in getting something
senses.definition: to succeed in obtaining a job, a contract or an opportunity
senses.definitionCN: 成功得到工作、合同或机会
senses.example: He landed a good job at a design studio.
senses.exampleCN: 他在一家设计工作室找到了一份好工作。
senses.why: To land a job is to bring something down and secure it, like a plane touching the ground after a search.
senses.whyCN: land a job 就像飞机经过搜寻后触地一样，把某样东西稳稳弄到手。

intro.en: Land is an Old English word shared across the Germanic languages, with a deep but partly reconstructed root.
intro.cn: land 是古英语词，在日耳曼语族中广泛共享，其更深词根有一部分属于重构形式。

items.en: Land meant earth, territory or a country, and it already carried both the physical and the political sense.
items.cn: land 意为土地、领土或国家，已经同时带有自然与政治两层意思。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form *landa is shared by German Land and Dutch land.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形式 *landa 为德语 Land 与荷兰语 land 所共享。

items.en: The deeper root is reconstructed as *lendh-, meaning land or heath, but the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 更深的词根被重构为 *lendh-，意为土地或荒地，但这一重构并不确定。

items.en: Middle English keeps land for ground and country and begins to use it as a verb for coming ashore.
items.cn: 中古英语保留 land 表示土地与国家，并开始把它用作「上岸」的动词。

items.en: Modern English adds landing, landscape and landlord, and extends the verb to planes and jobs.
items.cn: 现代英语添上 landing、landscape、landlord，并把动词扩展到飞机与工作。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on land; the near-meaning group gathers words for ground, country and coming down.
note.cn: 形近组收以 land 构成的词；近义组收表示土地、国家与降落的词。

normalIntro.en: One short Germanic word covers ground, country and the act of touching down, and its compounds make the connections visible.
normalIntro.cn: 一个简短的日耳曼词同时覆盖土地、国家与触地，复合词把这些联系摆了出来。

normal.en: Land is both noun and verb: the land, to land.
normal.cn: land 名动同形：the land 与 to land。

normal.cn: landscape 把 land 与表示景色的 -scape 组合。

normal.en: Landlord joins land to lord: the owner of the ground.
normal.cn: landlord 把 land 与 lord 组合，指土地的主人。

normal.en: Landing adds -ing and names both the act and the place where you step down.
normal.cn: landing 加 -ing，既指着陆动作，也指落脚的平台。

normal.en: To land a job keeps the idea of a plane touching down after a search.
normal.cn: land a job 保留飞机经过搜寻后触地的意象。

abstract.en: The same word serves soil, nation and arrival because all three are places where movement stops.
abstract.cn: 同一个词同时服务泥土、国家与抵达，因为三者都是运动停下来的地方。

abstract.en: Owning land turns a physical surface into a legal and emotional object.
abstract.cn: 拥有土地把一个物理表面变成为法律与情感的对象。

abstract.en: A landing is a boundary event: above and below meet for a moment.
abstract.cn: landing 是一个边界事件：上与下短暂地相接。

definition_zh: 尊敬；荣誉；光荣；荣幸；（动词）尊敬；给……荣誉
definition_en: great respect, or a special mark of respect; as a verb, to show respect for someone or something
core_image: 一枚别在胸前的奖章：被众人抬高的那个名字

senses.title: Great respect
senses.definition: the respect that people show to someone they admire
senses.definitionCN: 人们对值得敬佩者所表达的敬重
senses.example: The old teacher was held in honour by three generations.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老教师受到三代人的敬重。
senses.why: The medal image is respect made visible: a name lifted above the crowd.
senses.whyCN: 奖章意象是让尊敬看得见：把一个名字抬到人群之上。

senses.title: A mark or prize of respect
senses.definition: something given to show respect, such as a prize or a title
senses.definitionCN: 用来表达尊敬的东西，如奖项、称号
senses.example: She brought honour to her school by winning the contest.
senses.exampleCN: 她赢得比赛，为学校争得了荣誉。
senses.why: What begins as a feeling can be pinned on the chest as a thing.
senses.whyCN: 尊敬从一种感受，变成一枚可以别在胸前的实体。

senses.title: The proud feeling of being respected
senses.definition: the proud and pleased feeling when you are given special respect
senses.definitionCN: 受到特殊礼遇时的自豪与喜悦
senses.example: It is a great honour to speak here today.
senses.exampleCN: 今天能在这里发言，我深感荣幸。
senses.why: When respect flows toward you, the feeling inside is honour.
senses.whyCN: 当尊敬流向你时，心里涌起的感受就是荣幸。

senses.title: To respect or keep a promise (verb)
senses.definition: to show respect for someone, or to do what you promised
senses.definitionCN: 对某人表示尊敬，或履行承诺
senses.example: The team honoured their promise to visit the old school.
senses.exampleCN: 球队履行了回访母校的承诺。
senses.why: A promise is treated like a flag: you raise it, and then you must keep it flying.
senses.whyCN: 承诺像旗帜：升起来之后，就必须让它一直飘着。

intro.en: Honour came through Old French onor from Latin honos, honour, the same root as honest.
intro.cn: honour 经古法语 onor 来自拉丁 honos「荣誉」，与 honest 同根。

items.en: Latin honos, later honor, meant public respect and official position.
items.cn: 拉丁 honos（后作 honor）指公众敬重与官职地位。

items.en: Old French onor carried the word into English after the Norman Conquest.
items.cn: 诺曼征服后，古法语 onor 把这个词带入英语。

items.en: Middle English spelled it honour under French influence; American English later cut the u.
items.cn: 受法语影响，中古英语拼作 honour；美式英语后来删去 u。

items.en: Modern English widened the verb: honour people, honour promises, honour the dead.
items.cn: 现代英语扩展了动词用法：尊敬人、信守承诺、缅怀逝者。

items.en: The same Latin root builds honest, honorary and honorarium.
items.cn: 同一拉丁词根还派生出 honest、honorary 与 honorarium。

note.en: Group one keeps the silent-h same-root family; group two keeps words for respect and glory.
note.cn: 第一组是 h 不发音的同根词族；第二组是表示尊敬与荣耀的近义词。
